quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: After drinking alcohol, what reduces its effects?

options.text: Exercise
Coffee
Time
Food

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. You cannot speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects on your body.

questions.question: Where is a motorcycle most likely to have a conflict with other traffic?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Be extra careful when another vehicle might cross in front of you.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Always use your headlight.
Wave your arms.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight.
questions.explanation: To be more visible at an intersection, ride with your headlight on. Position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep space between you and other vehicles so you can escape if danger appears. Do not rely on eye contact alone—drivers may not notice you.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT do to ride safely at night?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Use high beam headlights when possible.
Keep a larger distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, use high beams when no other vehicles are near, and keep more distance between you and other vehicles. Watch the vehicles ahead—their lights show you the road and alert you to bumps.

questions.question: What should rain suits do?

options.text: Should not be used.
Not puff up or balloon when you ride.
Are not needed because motorcycles should not ride in rain.
Should tear easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not puff up or balloon when you ride.
questions.explanation: Good motorcycle rain suits will not tear or balloon up when you ride at high speeds.

questions.question: Why is riding directly beside another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
It is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
It is safe because you have limited escape routes.
You should only do this during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Never ride directly beside another vehicle. The driver may not see you in their blind spot and could move into your lane. Riding beside a vehicle also blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Why use both front and rear brakes every time you stop?

options.text: Using one brake causes uneven wear.
It builds the habit of using both brakes in emergencies.
Both brakes are the only way to slow a motorcycle.
Brakes only work when both are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds the habit of using both brakes in emergencies.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes during normal stops builds the habit. This habit is important in emergencies, where using both brakes may be critical to staying safe.

questions.question: Which foot operates the gearshift lever?

options.text: Right hand
Right foot
Left hand
Left foot

questions.correctAnswerText: Left foot
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal, check mirrors, and turn your head.
Signal and check mirrors.
Turn your head and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Use your mirrors and check over your shoulder to see traffic around you.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride through a curve?

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a single-file formation.
In a side-by-side formation.
Using both lanes if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Groups should ride in single-file formation when going through curves, making turns, entering highways, or leaving highways. A staggered formation is used on straightaways.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Not worry about where you position yourself.
Always ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when behind a car. The driver will most likely see you in the rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: To help a driver merge from an entrance ramp into your lane, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Move to the next lane if you can.
Do nothing, since they are the ones merging.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the next lane if you can.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Move to another lane if possible to give them safe space to merge.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing?

options.text: A leather jacket
Full-fingered gloves
Long pants made of denim
Athletic shoes

questions.correctAnswerText: Athletic shoes
questions.explanation: A leather jacket, long denim pants, and full-fingered gloves all protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or heavy shoes that support your ankles instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees that the driver will yield to you.
Is not worth your effort.
Does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
Always means the driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that making eye contact with a driver means they will give you the right-of-way. Never count on it.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid hitting an object or uneven surface, you should:

options.text: Make sure your motorcycle is leaning to one side.
Speed up.
Swerve quickly.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, approach it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as possible. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off the seat so your knees can absorb the shock. Just before contact, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle:

options.text: Lets you touch the ground with your feet while seated.
Has a seat level with your waist.
Has a seat 10 inches above your waist.
Has a seat 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you touch the ground with your feet while seated.
questions.explanation: Your feet should be able to reach the ground when you are seated on your motorcycle. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests while riding.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles helps because:

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You have a narrower view so you stay focused.
You have more time to react to other vehicles.
You can follow the next vehicle more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Maintaining space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more space to maneuver around them.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes involve:

options.text: Speeds greater than 35 mph.
Nighttime riding.
Worn tires.
Riders with less than six months of experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with less than six months of experience.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle. Most crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a way to stop a friend from driving while intoxicated?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Keep them busy with activities to slow their drinking.
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Ask other friends to help stop them from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: To prevent drunk driving, arrange another way for them to get home, keep them busy with activities to slow their drinking, use any excuse to keep them from leaving, and get friends to help.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle operator check their mirrors?

options.text: Never
Once in a while
Often
More than the time you spend looking ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Often
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see hazards behind you.

questions.question: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go over it as slowly as possible.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Less maintenance than a car.
More maintenance than a car.
Pre-ride checks performed only by a mechanic.
Service only at a dealer.

questions.correctAnswerText: More maintenance than a car.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle more often. Do a full check before every ride.

questions.question: When riding at night instead of during the day, a motorcycle operator should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride more slowly.
Stay farther away from other vehicles.
Use high beams when possible.
Follow closely behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow closely behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, slow down and increase the space between you and other vehicles. Use the lights of other vehicles to see ahead. Change your lane position when needed, especially at night.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should travel:

options.text: More slowly than during the day in similar conditions.
At the same speed as during the day in similar conditions.
Faster than during the day in similar conditions.
On the road shoulder so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than during the day in similar conditions.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, go slower than you would during the day in similar weather and traffic. It is harder to see hazards in the dark. Slowing down helps you avoid dangers.
